reason: Conversation 1 stayed within neutral, non-endorsing buying criteria (capacity, spin, depth, warranty) and proactively asked what actually happened to the old machine, which uncovered the humming/no-drain symptom that points to a likely free pump-filter fix; its draining guidance was thorough and safe (unplug, slow trickle via emergency hose or cap, don't force panels or the door, refit filter straight, impeller should have slight magnetic resistance). Conversation 2 endorsed specific brands (including Miele, unrealistic under £400) rather than deferring to independent reviews, only pivoted to diagnosis when the customer raised it, gave thinner draining instructions, and then asked the same two questions repeatedly without adding value. Both correctly insisted on unplugging first, but Conversation 1 handled scope, diagnosis and safety better overall.
